title: A weaker shield needs more people
hook: A perfect vaccine needs 75% covered here. What about one that works 80% as well?

knows: the herd-immunity threshold is 1 - 1/R0 for a perfect vaccine
doesNotKnow: that with an imperfect vaccine the coverage needed is (1 - 1/R0) / efficacy
that below a certain efficacy no coverage is enough on its own

misconception: The vaccine coverage needed depends only on R0.
objective: The learner can explain that a vaccine that cuts infection chance by 80% needs 0.75 / 0.8, about 94%, coverage when R0 = 4, and that below 75% efficacy even full coverage leaves R above 1.

claims.text: With R0 = 4, a perfect vaccine needs 1 - 1/4 = 75% coverage; a vaccine of efficacy e needs (1 - 1/R0) / e, so 80% efficacy needs 0.75 / 0.8 = 93.75%, about 94%.
claims.source: Anderson R.M. & May R.M. (1991) Infectious Diseases of Humans, Oxford UP, ch. 5 (critical coverage with imperfect vaccines). Arithmetic in Demo.tsx (needed).

claims.text: At 70% efficacy the needed coverage would be 107%, impossible; even 100% coverage leaves R = 4 x (1 - 0.7) = 1.2. Any efficacy below 75% gives a needed coverage above 100% when R0 = 4.
At the start of an outbreak in a well-mixed population, R = R0 x (1 - coverage x efficacy), whether the vaccine is leaky (cuts everyone's chance by e) or all-or-nothing (fully protects a share e).
claims.source: Susceptibility of the vaccinated is 1 - e in either case on average; the two types differ later in an outbreak, not in initial R (Halloran, Longini & Struchiner 2010, Design and Analysis of Vaccine Studies, ch. 2).

claims.text: The model is a made-up disease and vaccine with random mixing; it is not a statement about any real vaccine.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; stated in the question ('Made-up disease'), on the stage ('Toy town') and in the reveal.

recall.question: A made-up disease has R0 = 5, so a perfect vaccine would need 80% coverage. A vaccine cuts infection chance by 90%. Roughly what coverage is needed?
recall.why: Coverage needed = (1 - 1/R0) / efficacy = 0.8 / 0.9, about 89%: a weaker shield needs more people under it.
